notes.title: News Korean
notes.text: Anchors use the formal -ㅂ니다 / -습니다 style: 안녕하십니까 (good evening), 늘어났습니다 (has increased). N에 따르면 means "according to": 뉴스에 따르면 (according to the news). Korea has one of the world's lowest birth rates — a constant topic on the news.

notes.title: Environment words
notes.text: 환경 (environment), 지구 (the Earth), 공기 (air), 에너지 (energy), 전기 (electricity), 석유 (oil), 가스 (gas). Korea takes recycling (분리수거) seriously — food waste, plastics, cans and paper each go in their own bin. 변하다 and 바뀌다 both mean "to change."

notes.title: -(으)ㄴ/는 반면에
notes.text: -는 반면에 (verbs) and -(으)ㄴ 반면에 (adjectives) set two facts against each other: 전기 차는 환경에 좋은 반면에 비싸요 (electric cars are good for the environment, but they're expensive). It's a little formal — perfect for weighing 장점 (pros) against 단점 (cons).

notes.title: Formal connectors
notes.text: Written Korean uses connectors you rarely hear in chat: 즉 (that is), 그러므로 (therefore), 또한 (also, furthermore), 및 (and — on forms: 이름 및 연락처), 내지 (from … to: 한 시간 내지 두 시간). 의미 and 뜻 both mean "meaning"; 무슨 뜻이에요? is how you ask "What does it mean?"

notes.title: Getting bigger, getting smaller
notes.text: Adjective + -아/어지다 means "become": 커지다 (get bigger), 작아지다 (get smaller), 많아지다 (increase), 적어지다 (decrease), 짧아지다 (get shorter), 넓어지다 (get wider). 공사 중 (under construction) signs are everywhere in fast-changing Seoul.

notes.title: Formal vocabulary
notes.text: Sino-Korean words make speech sound polished: 국제 (international), 각국 (each country), 각종 (all kinds of), 주요 (main), 대표적 (classic, representative), 일반적 (general, typical), 공동 (joint). 등 means "and so on" (음식, 노래, 춤 등) and also "place, rank" (1등 = first place).
